rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ihsar is not causative here, it means becoming or being found detained; lexicographers reserve mahsur for one blocked by an enemy, supporting the enemy-only reading.
rows.anchor: أهل اللغة أتفقوا على أن المحصور هو الممنوع بالعدو لا بالمرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being prevented presupposes capacity to act; illness removes that capacity, whereas an enemy obstructs someone capable of acting, so ihsar properly denotes enemy obstruction.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن لفظة الاحصار حقيقة في العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Detention and prevention require an agent; illness is an accident and cannot literally act as a jailer, while an enemy can truly detain and prevent.
rows.anchor: لأن الحبس والمنع فعل ، وإضافة الفعل إلى المرض محال عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the root hasr carries no indication of illness, its derived form ihsar should likewise not imply illness.
rows.anchor: أن الإحصار مشتق من الحصر ولفظ الحصر لا إشعار فيه بالمرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse separately mentions illness after ihsar; taking ihsar to include illness would make the coordination repeat the same category.
rows.anchor: فعطف عليه المريض ، فلو كان المحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed reply says illness is repeated because it has a distinct rule for shaving, but al-Razi says this still leaves illness coordinated with itself.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه مع ذلك يلزم عطف الشيء على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unqualified security is security from an enemy, not recovery from illness; the unqualified phrase therefore supports enemy-blocking as the meaning of ihsar.
rows.anchor: لفظ الأمن إذا كان مطلقا غير مقيد فإنه لا يفيد إلا الأمن من العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse does not name what people become safe from, “when you are safe” refers back to the previously mentioned ihsar, hence to safety from enemy obstruction.
rows.anchor: قوله : { فإذا أمنتم } ليس فيه بيان أنه حصل الأمن مماذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes agree the occasion was the polytheists' blockade of the Prophet at Hudaybiyya; the revealed occasion cannot fall outside the verse, excluding an illness-only sense.
rows.anchor: أن المفسرين أجمعوا على أن سبب نزول هذه الآية أن الكفار أحصروا النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi concludes ihsar here means enemy obstruction alone and rejects analogy from illness because the conditional wording confines the ruling to the stated case; extending it would abrogate the text by analogy.
rows.anchor: فلو أثبتا هذا الحكم في غيره قياسا كان ذلك نسخا للنص بالقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness cannot be analogized to enemy blockade because ihram is binding and is not deliberately annulled: intercourse that invalidates hajj and missing hajj requiring make-up do not end ihram.
rows.anchor: الإحرام شرع لازم لا يحتمل النسخ قصدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ill pilgrim gains no safety from illness by returning, while a person blocked by enemies can escape fear of being killed by turning back; this is another reason the cases differ.
rows.anchor: المريض لا يستفيد بتحلله ورجوعه أمنا من مرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal supplies an ellipsis in the blocked-pilgrim clause: after becoming blocked, the pilgrim is released and offers what animal is available, as in the ellipsis in 2:184.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : فحللتم فما استيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the incomplete phrase can mean either that what is available is obligatory, or that the pilgrim is commanded to offer what is available; al-Farra permits the accusative, though Qur'anic parallels are usually nominative.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : لو نصبت على معنى : اهدوا ما تيسر كان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ista ysara means tayassara, just as istaʿẓama means taʿaẓẓama, istakbara means takabbara, and istaṣʿaba means taṣaʿʿaba.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثانية : { استيسر } بمعنى تيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains al-hady as the plural of hadiya, like tamr/tamra; Ahmad ibn Yahya says the Hijaz lightens the form while Tamim pronounces it heavily.
rows.anchor: أحمد بن يحيى : أهل الحجاز يخففون { الهدى } وتميم تثقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's line uses al-hady for sacrificial animals whose necks are garlanded; al-Razi defines hady as what is offered to God's House as an act of nearness, like a human gift.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الهدي : ما يهدى إلى بيت الله عز وجل تقربا إليه

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They rank the sacrificial animals from highest to lowest as camel, cow, and sheep, so the pilgrim owes whichever of these is available.
rows.anchor: قال علي وابن عباس والحسن وقتادة : الهدي أعلاه بدنة

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: One Shafi'i position, also held by Abu Hanifa, gives a blocked pilgrim no substitute for the animal: it remains a debt because the verse specifies hady and names no replacement.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : لا بدل له ويكون الهدي في ذمته أبدا

rows.speaker: أحمد
rows.claim: A second Shafi'i position, also attributed to Ahmad, allows a substitute for the hady.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن له بدلا ينتقل إليه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: If no substitute is allowed, Abu Hanifa says the pilgrim remains in ihram until an animal becomes available, following the apparent verse.
rows.anchor: أنه يقيم على إحرامه حتى يجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi regards immediate release as the stronger view because of hardship; if a substitute is allowed, the closest option is to value the hady in money, buy food, and give it.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يتحلل في الحال للمشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A blocked pilgrim who intends to leave ihram must intend release when slaughtering and cannot leave ihram before slaughter.
rows.anchor: ولا يتحلل البتة قبل الذبح

rows.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
rows.claim: Most jurists give umrah the same rule as hajj concerning ihsar.
rows.anchor: أكثر الفقهاء قالوا حكمها في الإحصار كحكم الحج

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin denies ihsar applies to umrah because it is not restricted to a fixed time; al-Razi rejects this because the verse follows mention of both hajj and umrah.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن سيرين أنه لا إحصار فيه لأنه غير مؤقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits a step: reaching the animal's place does not itself release the pilgrim; the animal must be slaughtered, after which shaving is allowed.
rows.anchor: لا يحصل التحلل إلا بالنحر

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i permits the blocked pilgrim to slaughter where detained; he reads mahill as the time at which release occurs.
rows.anchor: يجوز إراقة دم الإحصار لا في الحرم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires slaughter in the Haram; he reads mahill as a place.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز ذلك إلا في الحرم ومنشأ الخلاف البحث في تفسير هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i's first proof is that the Prophet, blocked at Hudaybiyya, slaughtered there; Hanafis answer that the place was at the Haram's edge, and al-Waqidi places it nine miles from Mecca.
rows.anchor: إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أحصر بالحديبية ونحر بها

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal answers that Qur'an 48:25 says the polytheists prevented the Prophet from bringing the animal to its intended place, showing it was slaughtered outside the Haram.
rows.anchor: هم الذين كفروا وصدوكم عن المسجد الحرام والهدى معكوفا أن يبلغ محله

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The verse addresses every blocked pilgrim in the open country or the Haram and requires an available animal; therefore the pilgrim must be able to slaughter wherever blocked.
rows.anchor: يتناول كل من كان محصرا سواء كان في الحل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The verse's purpose is immediate release from the enemy's danger; requiring the animal to reach the Haram would prevent immediate release, and an intermediary might not be available.
rows.anchor: مكن المحصر من التحلل بالذبح ليتمكن من تخليص النفس عن خوف العدو في الحال

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that mahill, with the verbal noun's kasra, denotes a place, so the command says the animal must reach the place of release; al-Razi replies that mahill can mean a time, as in a debt's due date.
rows.anchor: أن المحل بكسر عين الفعل عبارة عن المكان

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa cites 22:33 and 5:95, which direct offerings to the Ancient House or the Kaaba and thus, he argues, to the Haram.
rows.anchor: ثم محلها إلى البيت العتيق

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa also cites the description of an offering as reaching the Kaaba as evidence for sacrifice in the Haram.
rows.anchor: هديا بالغ الكعبة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i answers that those verses concern ordinary offerings, while an enemy-blocked pilgrim is an exception and slaughters where detained; he also names a second exception for a pilgrim who drives an offering and must divert it on the way.
rows.anchor: كل ما وجب على المحرم في ماله من بدنة وجزاء هدي فلا يجزي إلا في الحرم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Hanafi argument says hady is named after a gift sent by a worshipper to God, which counts as a gift only when sent to the recipient's abode, the Haram.
rows.anchor: والهدية لا تكون هدية إلا إذا بعثها المهدي إلى دار المهدى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that pilgrims should not leave ihram and shave until they first offer whatever hady is available, just as the Prophet required charity before private consultation.
rows.anchor: لا ينبغي لهم أن يحلوا فيحلقوا رؤوسهم إلا بعد تقديم ما استيسر من الهدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse was revealed about Ka'b ibn ʿUjra: at Hudaybiyya the Prophet noticed lice and nits falling from Ka'b's hair, asked whether the vermin troubled him, and ordered him to shave.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : نزلت هذه الآية في كعب بن عجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling permits a pilgrim in ihram to treat an illness or shave for bothersome head vermin, provided he pays the prescribed compensation.
rows.anchor: المحرم إذا تأذى بالمرض أو بهوام رأسه أبيح له المداواة والحلق بشرط الفدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fidya is nominative as the subject with an omitted predicate, “upon him is fidya”; an additional ellipsis supplies “if he shaves.”
rows.anchor: ففدية رفع لأنه مبتدأ خبره محذوف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation makes this provision specific to a muhsar who develops illness or head trouble before the hady arrives, allowing the needed act for fidya.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : هذه الآية مختصة بالمحصر

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation treats the passage as a new general rule for any pilgrim who becomes ill and needs treatment or has head trouble and needs shaving, with fidya specified.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون بل الكلام مستأنف لكل محرم لحقه المرض في بدنه فاحتاج إلى علاج

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i answers that the argument from the name shows the preferred location when ability permits, not a condition for validity.
rows.anchor: هذا التمسك بالاسم ثم هو محمول على الأفضل عند القدرة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Hanafi argument adds that other pilgrimage offerings, devotional or expiatory, are valid only in the Haram, so this one should be too.
rows.anchor: الرابع : أن سائر دماء الحج كلها قربة كانت أو كفارة لا تصح إلا في الحرم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i distinguishes this offering because it removes fear only if the blocked pilgrim can slaughter where detained; that purpose does not apply to the other offerings.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الدم إنما وجب لإزالة الخوف وزوال الخوف إنما يحصل إذا قدر عليه حيث أحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concession extends to other prohibited acts: illness may require clothing or perfume, and cold can require clothing; these acts are permitted subject to fidya.
rows.anchor: المرض قد يحوج إلى اللباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Head trouble can come from lice, nits, headache, or fear of impending illness or pain; al-Razi generalizes the rule to all hajj prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة فهذا الحكم عام في جميع محظورات الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although jurists differ whether fidya precedes or follows taking the concession, al-Razi prefers paying after: the act that triggers the compensation comes first, as the ellipsis “he shaves, then fidya is due” shows.
rows.anchor: والذي يقتضيه الظاهر أنه يؤخر الفدية عن الترخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nusk originally means worship; Ibn al-A'rabi derives it from refined silver ingots, and a worshipper is called nasik because he purifies himself from sins like refined silver; slaughter is then called nusk as a noble act of worship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي النسك سبائك الفضة كل سبيكة منها نسيكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists agree that the minimum nusuk is a sheep: the eligible animals are camel, cow, and sheep, and the sheep is the smallest.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا في النسك على أن أقله شاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not specify the amount or method of fasting or feeding; one view takes their details from Ka'b ibn ʿUjra's report in Abu Dawud: a sheep, three days of fasting, or three saʿs of dates for six poor people.
rows.anchor: احلق ثم اذبح شاة نسكا أو صم ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: A second view from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan says fasting or feeding follows the tamattu measure of ten days; since the verse leaves both unspecified, they take their detail from the later tamattu ruling.
rows.anchor: يروى عن ابن عباس والحسن أنهما قالا : الصيام للمتمتع عشرة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the first specification is followed by most jurists.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول عليه أكثر الفقهاء

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifa require a blood offering from someone who deliberately shaves without excuse; Malik gives him the same ruling as a person excused by illness or head harm.
rows.anchor: فعند الشافعي رضي الله عنه وأبي حنيفة الواجب عليه الدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects Malik's equal treatment of deliberate shaving because the verse conditions fidya on illness or head harm; a conditional ruling does not apply when its condition is absent.
rows.anchor: يدل على اشتراط هذا الحكم بهذه الأعذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When you are safe” means safe from ihsar.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أن تقديره : فإذا أمنتم من الإحصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamattu means taking pleasure; the word matāʿ refers to something enjoyed, and the root is associated with length, as in a long rope and prolonged companionship.
rows.anchor: معنى التمتع التلذذ ، يقال : تمتع بالشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valid, non-disliked tamattu is to arrive in Mecca, perform umrah in the hajj months, remain out of ihram, and perform hajj there in the same year; it is called tamattu because prohibitions lapse between the rites.
rows.anchor: فيعتمر في أشهر الحج ، ثم يقيم بمكة حلالا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar warned against and threatened punishment for two mut'as practiced in the Prophet's time: temporary marriage and hajj-mut'a.
rows.anchor: متعتان كانتا على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا أنهي عنهما وأعاقب عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disfavored hajj-mut'a is to combine the two ihrams and then dissolve hajj into umrah; reports say the Prophet first allowed this for his companions and later abrogated it.
rows.anchor: أن يجمع بين الإحرامين ثم يفسخ الحج إلى العمرة

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports that hajj-mut'a was only for the Prophet's companions: he used it to overturn their belief that umrah during hajj months was abominable, so the special reason for transferring them from hajj to umrah did not apply to others.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي ذر أنه قال : ما كانت متعة الحج إلا لي خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Enjoying umrah” means enjoying the lifting of ihram prohibitions because one performed umrah before hajj.
rows.anchor: فمن يتمتع بسبب العمرة فكأنه لا يتمتع بالعمرة ولكنه يتمتع بمحظورات الإحرام بسبب إتيانه بالعمرة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The first condition for tamattu compensation is that umrah precede hajj.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن يقدم العمرة على الحج

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The second condition is that umrah ihram begin in the hajj months; if it begins earlier and even one circumambulation is done before those months, completing umrah in the months and doing hajj that year incurs no dam.
rows.anchor: أن يحرم بالعمرة في أشهر الحج

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: If ihram begins before the hajj months but the umrah acts occur in them, al-Shafi'i's position in al-Umm, which al-Razi calls sounder, imposes no dam because an umrah pillar occurred before the months.
rows.anchor: وهو الأصح : لا يلزمه دم التمتع لأنه أتى بركن

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i's older and al-Imlaʾ position imposes dam when ihram starts before the months but is continued into them, treating continuation as a fresh beginning.
rows.anchor: وقال في ( القديم والإملاء ) : يلزمه ذلك ويجعل استدامة الإحرام

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa counts the pilgrim as mutamatti if some but not most of the circumambulation occurred before the hajj months.
rows.anchor: إذا أتى ببعض الطواف قبل أشهر الحج فهو متمتع إذا لم يأت بأكثره

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The third condition is that hajj occur in the same year; otherwise there is no dam because the two rites did not compete in one year.
rows.anchor: أن يحج في هذه السنة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The fourth condition is not being among the Haram's residents: those living nearer than the distance of a shortened journey count as present, while the measurement is disputed between Mecca and the Haram.
rows.anchor: وحاضر المسجد الحرام من كان أهله على مسافة أقل من مسافة القصر

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The fifth condition is beginning hajj ihram inside Mecca after umrah; returning to the miqat removes dam because the pilgrim has not omitted ihram at the miqat.
rows.anchor: جوف مكة بعد الفراغ من العمرة فإن عاد إلى الميقات

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i classifies the tamattu blood as compensation for a deficiency and forbids eating it; Abu Hanifa calls it a devotional offering and permits eating it.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : دم التمتع دم جبران الإساءة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: When Uthman opposed tamattu, Ali answered that Uthman was suppressing a concession warranted by need and being a stranger, evidence for a deficiency in tamattu according to al-Shafi'i's argument.
rows.anchor: فقال له علي رضي الله عنهما : عمدت إلى رخصة بسبب الحاجة والغربة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i argues that the name tamattu, meaning indulgence and pleasure, signals a flaw because worship is founded on hardship.
rows.anchor: والتمتع عبارة عن التلذذ والإرتفاع

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i details the deficiency: travel should have been for the greater rite, hajj; the pilgrim enjoys a period out of ihram; and the miqat should have been assigned to hajj rather than umrah.
rows.anchor: أن في التمتع صار السفر للعمرة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Since dam is not an original rite when hajj and umrah are performed separately or for a Meccan resident, and combining acts of worship otherwise requires no blood, al-Shafi'i calls it compensation.
rows.anchor: أن الدم ليس بنسك أصلي من مناسك الحج أو العمرة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i argues that the tamattu hady has no specified time, unlike the timed rites, so it is compensatory rather than a devotional rite.
rows.anchor: وكونه غير مؤقت دليل على أنه دم جبران لأن المناسك كلها مؤقتة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i argues that fasting can replace this offering, whereas a devotional nusuk cannot be replaced by fasting.
rows.anchor: أن للصوم فيه مدخلا ، ودم النسك لا يبدل بالصوم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i reads the call to complete hajj and umrah as proof that tamattu hajj has a deficiency, which the hady repairs; al-Razi says this contextual reading works only on al-Shafi'i's view.
rows.anchor: ألزم المكلف إتمام الحج في قوله : { وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi concludes that this coherent reading of the verse supports al-Shafi'i's classification of the tamattu blood as compensation rather than a devotional rite.
rows.anchor: فهذا معنى حسن مفهوم من سياق الآية وهو لا يتقرر إلا على مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه
